bull.b: Strong cloud expansion, elevated remaining performance obligations and NRR above 120% indicate durable subscription demand, customer expansion and revenue visibility. These metrics support continued growth across Atlassian's recurring software base.

Sustained operating and free cash flow despite reported net losses demonstrates strong cash conversion from the subscription model. This provides funding for product investment, AI development and balance-sheet improvement without relying solely on external capital.

Rapid AI adoption and strong growth in large customer cohorts deepen Atlassian's role in enterprise workflows. Broader seat expansion, cross-sell and platform engagement can increase customer dependence and support durable recurring revenue growth.

bear.b: Ongoing GAAP losses and volatile operating profitability show that strong gross margins have not yet translated consistently into bottom-line earnings. Continued investment and cost pressure could limit retained cash earnings and shareholder returns.

The lower ARR outlook versus FY26 and reduced full-year margin guide imply that growth may normalize while investment and execution demands remain elevated. This could make durable operating leverage harder to achieve over the next several quarters.

Although leverage has improved materially, debt remains sizable relative to equity and negative ROE reflects continuing accounting losses. This reduces balance-sheet flexibility and could constrain strategic investment if cash generation weakens.
